intro: To check the Xcode version in Xcode on Mac, open the app and select About Xcode from the main menu bar. This window displays the full version number and the specific build identifier for your installation.
tldr: Click the Xcode menu in the top left corner.
Select About Xcode to see the version and build number.
Use the xcodebuild -version command in Terminal for command-line verification.
Ensure you are running Xcode 27 or later for the latest Apple silicon compatibility.

blocks.text: Why checking your Xcode version matters

Maintaining the correct Xcode version is essential for smooth development. Apple updates its SDKs regularly to support new hardware and software features. If you build apps for iOS, watchOS, or visionOS, your IDE version must meet the minimum requirements for App Store submissions. Using an outdated version can trigger errors during the build process or prevent your app from passing the initial validation checks. Developers often encounter issues when they try to compile code using features that are only available in newer SDKs. By knowing your current version, you can decide if it is time to perform an update via the Mac App Store.
How to check the Xcode version in Xcode on Mac using the menu

The simplest method to find your version is through the standard Mac interface. This approach provides the most accurate build number. You might need this build number when reporting bugs to Apple or when troubleshooting with your team.

items: Launch the Xcode application from your Applications folder or via Spotlight search.
Locate the menu bar at the very top of your display.
Click on the word Xcode positioned to the right of the Apple icon.
Select About Xcode from the dropdown menu that appears.
A small window will open showing the version number, such as 27.1, and the specific build number in parentheses.

blocks.text: Command line access is often faster for developers who spend their time in the terminal. You can quickly verify which version of Xcode is active on your system. This is especially helpful if you have installed multiple versions of Xcode to test legacy projects or beta releases.

Open your terminal application and type the following command: xcodebuild -version. Press Enter. The terminal will output the version and build information for the currently active developer path. If you need to verify the path itself, run xcode-select -p. This command confirms exactly which directory your system is using to run Xcode tools.

Developers often keep older versions of Xcode on their Macs. You might need an older version to maintain a legacy project or to verify how an app behaves on an older SDK. If you have multiple versions installed, you must tell your Mac which one to use for command line tasks. Use the sudo xcode-select --switch command followed by the full path to the specific Xcode app folder. This ensures that your build tools and simulators point to the correct version.

If you receive an error about a missing developer directory, run xcode-select --install in your terminal. This command triggers the installation of the necessary command line tools, which often fixes common environment path issues.
blocks.title: Fixing common setup issues

blocks.text: Updating Xcode through the App Store

The Mac App Store is the official channel for Xcode updates. Open the App Store and search for Xcode to see if a newer version is available. Click the Update button if you see one. Always verify your available disk space before you start the update. Xcode is a large application and requires significant space for the download and the installation process. Keeping your IDE updated ensures you have the latest performance improvements and security patches for your development environment.

faq.question: Is there a web-based version of Xcode?
faq.answer: No. Xcode is a native macOS application. There is no official web app version. Services like Xcode Cloud are cloud-based CI/CD tools that integrate with the native app, but they do not replace the local IDE.

faq.question: Does Xcode 27 run on Intel Macs?
faq.answer: No. Xcode 27 requires an Apple silicon Mac. Users with Intel-based Macs must use older versions of Xcode, such as Xcode 26, for their development work.

faq.question: How do I find my build number?
faq.answer: You can find the build number in the About Xcode window. It is listed in parentheses next to the main version number.

steps.name: Open Xcode
steps.text: Launch Xcode from your Applications folder or use Spotlight search by pressing ⌘ Space and typing Xcode.

steps.name: Access the About menu
steps.text: Click on the Xcode menu in the top menu bar, then select About Xcode.

steps.name: Read the version
steps.text: View the version and build number in the window that appears on your screen.

troubleshooting.problem: Unable to get active developer directory
troubleshooting.fix: Run xcode-select --install in your Terminal to install the necessary command line tools.

troubleshooting.problem: Wrong Xcode version active in Terminal
troubleshooting.fix: Use sudo xcode-select --switch followed by the path to your preferred Xcode app to change the active version.
